Longitudinal section of a human molar tooth fixed in the jaw bone, shown large and centred. Show the crown with two cusps above the gum, the narrow neck at gum level, and two roots inside the jaw bone. Inside, show the outer white enamel layer over the crown, the thick cream-coloured dentine under it, the central pink pulp cavity extending down into each root as root canals, with red blood vessels and yellow nerves entering through a small opening at the tip of each root. Show the thin cement layer covering the roots, the periodontal membrane (fibres) between the cement and the bone, and pink gum covering the jaw bone around the neck.

Two diagrams of the human upper and lower jaws seen from above (occlusal view), side by side. Left: a child's jaws with 20 milk teeth, colour-coded: incisors (blue), canines (green), milk molars (orange). Right: an adult's jaws with 32 permanent teeth, colour-coded: incisors (blue), canines (green), premolars (yellow), molars (orange), with the third molars (wisdom teeth) shaded lighter.

Side view of a sheep's skull with the jaws slightly apart. Show the horny dental pad at the front of the upper jaw with no upper front teeth; the lower jaw with forward-sloping chisel-shaped incisors and an incisor-like canine; a wide toothless gap (diastema) behind the front teeth in both jaws; and a row of tall cheek teeth (premolars and molars) at the back. Add a small inset showing the grinding surface of a sheep molar from above with crescent-shaped enamel ridges.

Side view of a dog's skull with the jaws slightly open, showing small front incisors, long curved pointed upper and lower canines, pointed premolars, the large blade-like carnassial teeth (upper last premolar and lower first molar) highlighted in red, and small flattened molars behind them. Add a small inset showing the upper and lower carnassials sliding past each other like scissor blades.

Three skulls side by side in side view for comparison: a sheep (herbivore), a dog (carnivore) and a human (omnivore). Colour-code the teeth in all three: incisors (blue), canines (green), premolars (yellow), molars (orange), carnassials outlined in red on the dog. Show the dental pad and diastema on the sheep. Under each skull, a small curved arrow shows the main jaw movement: side to side for the sheep, up and down for the dog, up and down plus some side to side for the human.

Four longitudinal sections of a molar in a row showing the stages of dental caries. Stage 1: plaque on the enamel surface. Stage 2: a small dark cavity in the enamel. Stage 3: the cavity spreading into the dentine. Stage 4: the cavity reaching the pulp cavity, with an abscess (swelling of pus) at the root tip.
Side view of a human skull with the jaws slightly open, showing a continuous row of teeth without gaps. Colour-code the teeth: incisors (blue), canine (green), premolars (yellow), molars (orange).
